questions.enonce_markdown:
State the causative agent, a mode of transmission, two signs or two symptoms and two preventive measures of the following diseases:

(i) Gonorrhoea

(ii) Poliomyelitis

(iii) Typhoid fever. *(6,6,6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Disease | Causative agent | Mode of transmission | Signs / symptoms | Preventive measures |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **(i) Gonorrhoea** | The bacterium ***Neisseria gonorrhoeae*** | **Sexual intercourse** with an infected person; from an infected mother to the baby's eyes at birth | **Burning pain on urinating**; **yellowish pus-like discharge** from the penis or vagina (swelling of the groin) | Be **faithful to one uninfected partner** or abstain; **use condoms**; early **treatment of the patient and partner** with antibiotics; avoid multiple partners |
| **(ii) Poliomyelitis** | The **poliovirus** (a virus) | **Faeco-oral route**: food, water and hands contaminated with faeces of an infected person; also by droplets | **Fever, headache, stiff neck**, muscle pain; **paralysis** (usually of the legs) and wasting of muscles | **Vaccination** of children (oral polio vaccine) with booster doses; **good personal and environmental hygiene**, safe drinking water and proper disposal of faeces |
| **(iii) Typhoid fever** | The bacterium ***Salmonella typhi*** | Food and water **contaminated with faeces or urine** of a carrier or patient; by **flies**; dirty hands | **Prolonged high fever, headache, abdominal pain**, diarrhoea or constipation, rose-coloured spots on the chest, weakness | **Vaccination**; **wash hands**, boil drinking water, **wash food**, proper **sewage and refuse disposal**, control of flies, treat carriers |

Marking per disease (6 marks): causative agent 1, one mode of transmission 1, two signs or symptoms 2, two preventive measures 2.

questions.enonce_markdown: How do pathogens cause diseases? *(2 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Pathogens cause disease in two main ways:

1. They **multiply rapidly in the body**, destroying or damaging the **cells and tissues** that they invade (for example the poliovirus in nerve cells).
2. They **release poisonous substances (toxins)** into the body, which damage tissues or interfere with normal body functions (for example the toxins of the typhoid bacteria that cause fever).
